problem: Terminal exposed its server-rendered placeholders before client hydration and initial widget data. Startup JavaScript also queued behind busy local API connections.

observedBefore.chromiumAppCache: disabled to avoid suspended-renderer cache-entry locks

changes: Transport only the current loopback dashboard's public /_next/static/ assets through an Electron custom protocol, outside the API socket pool.
Share successful immutable assets in a 32 MiB bounded main-process cache; do not forward cookies or cache mutable/error responses.
Retain the outgoing page until a new Terminal document reports hydration and initial widget readiness, fonts and eager images settle, and its frame is ready.
Cancel pending handoffs when selection changes; retain immediate selection for already-ready Terminal documents and ordinary tabs.

verification.notes: Full initial-data readiness includes remote/widget latency. Hydration timing is not a promise of complete readiness. The original page remains visible during this wait. Actual-page checks used an isolated Electron session and the existing dashboard build; native reveal behavior was separately tested with controlled pending widgets/images.

applicationStatus: User chose to keep Breadboard open and apply later. Source and isolated test output updated; the running desktop is unchanged. Rebuild and restart are still required.
